transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me?

Well, I’ve been forgetting things I really shouldn’t be forgetting. Like I’ll miss a heart follow-up appointment, or forget to call the clinic back. Even small things—if I’m going to fix something, I’ll show up without the right tools. It’s happening enough that it’s starting to worry me.
Over the past few weeks, have you been feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy?
I don’t think so, no. I mean, I get frustrated with myself, but I haven’t really noticed feeling sad or losing interest in things.
How long have you been noticing these memory lapses, and have they been getting steadily worse over time, or have they stayed about the same?

I’d say it’s been a real problem for maybe a little over a year—about a year and a couple months. It seemed to start after my cardiac scare, when I had to cut back on the walking and little projects I used to do. I don’t know if it’s getting steadily worse, exactly, but it’s been sticking around and causing trouble.
Have these memory issues caused any problems with managing things like your medications, bills, or other daily responsibilities on your own?

Yeah, it has. I’m still trying to handle things myself, but it’s caused problems. The senior-center repair group I help with can’t really count on me like they used to, because I’ll forget things or not show up prepared. And my doctor’s office has had to call after me about missed heart follow-ups. That part worries me.

When you think back on the timeline, did your memory and thinking seem to get noticeably worse in sudden jumps—like right after your cardiac event—or has it been a slow, gradual decline the whole time?

It feels like it really started causing trouble after the cardiac scare, when I had to stop doing as much walking and those little projects that kept me steady. Since then—about a year and two months—it’s just been hanging around and causing problems. I wouldn’t say I noticed big sudden jumps after that, more that it’s stayed troublesome since then.

Besides forgetting things, have you noticed any new trouble finding the right words when speaking, getting confused about directions or familiar places, or difficulty planning and organizing tasks you used to handle easily?

No, not really. I haven’t noticed trouble with words or getting lost in places I know. Planning things… I mean, I can get a bit scattered, but I wouldn’t say it’s a new problem like that. It’s mostly the forgetting that I notice.
Are you still able to manage things like your finances, cooking, and other daily self-care completely on your own, or do you need someone else's help or reminders to get those done?

I’m mostly still doing things on my own, but it’s not as smooth as it used to be. The bigger problems show up with responsibilities outside the house—like the repair group at the senior center can’t really count on me like before, and my doctor’s office has had to call after me when I missed heart follow-ups. So I don’t have someone managing everything for me, but I do end up needing reminders or people chasing me on some important stuff.
